full_judgment:
3. After the death of Nagar Ali, though other heirs of Nagar Ali also became owners of the suit plot, there was amicable partition amongst all heirs for all properties, and the two daughters of Abdul Gafur viz, Alimun Nessa and minor Renu got the suit plot and that Nowab Ali, father of the plaintiff, purchased 6 decimals of the suit land from Alimun Nessa on 25-2-1946 and on 4-10-1951 he purchased another 3 decimals from Alimun Nessa and again on 5-10-1951 he purchased further 3 decimals from Alimun Nessa and Renu and that after the death of Nowab Ali the plaintiffs have become owners and have been living there constructing huts, cow sheds and growing vegetables, etc. But in the SA Record of rights, the defendants, in collusion with the settlement staff, have got their names recorded for 22 decimals. The plaintiffs filed Mutation Case No. 1310/8788 and the defendants raised objection and they started to threaten the plaintiffs with dispossession from 6 decimals of land and so the plaintiff filed the suit. 

 4. Defendants contested the suit by filing written statement and they claimed that the defendant No.1 purchased 3 decimals of land on 27-8-1956 from Renu on her attaining majority and another 5 decimals from two sisters on 27-8-1956 and another 7.5 decimals of land from Alimun Nessa alone on 20-10-1956 and thereafter defendant No.1 has exchanged and sold the lands with other defendants and they are in possession thereof for over 12 years and the suit is not maintainable in law in view of the fact that SA Record was prepared long before 6(six) years of filing of the suit which recorded possession of the land in the name of the defendants. 

 6. Dr Rafiqur Rahman, the learned Counsel, appearing on behalf of the leave petitioners argued that the High Court Division totally misconceived the nature of the dispute of the case, in view of the fact that SA record admittedly stands for 6 (six) decimals of land in the name of the plaintiffs and for 22 decimals of land in the name of the defendants and, in such view of the matter, the suit for declaration of title for 12(twelve) decimals is not maintainable without further prayer that SA record was wrongly prepared for 6 (six) decimals in the name of plaintiffs arid 22 decimals in the name of the defendants. It is further argued that the suit is barred by limitation as SA record was published long before 6 (six) years of the institution of the suit and plaintiffs did not come to court within the said period. This aspect having not been considered by the High Court Division there has been failure of justice. 

 8. The High Court Division also found that the lower appellate Court considered the oral evidence of PWs 1-4 and came to the conclusion that the plaintiffs have been in possession of 12 decimals of land out of28 decimals comprising Plot No. 128 and they are living in their dwelling hut standing thereon and they have been in possession for more than 30 (thirty) years. Since the possession of the plaintiffs has been proved by oral evidence and otherwise the suit is not barred by limitation for bringing the suit beyond 6 (six) years from the publication of the SA record.
